text:
maria_cs: FYI — Clearwave reported ~120 users lost assigned roles after an Okta org merge. They say some users are "ghost" members (appear in SCIM responses but no mapped role in our UI). Logs show several 403s during provisioning.

alex_support: Can you paste the SCIM PATCH payload and the relevant log snippets? Also do we have the token scopes for their Okta app?

maria_cs: Patch payload and minimal logs below:
```
PATCH /Groups/0e9a/members HTTP/1.1
Host: scim.redwood.example
Content-Type: application/scim+json
{ "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"], "Operations": [ { "op": "add", "path": "members", "value": [{"value":"00u1a2b3","display":"sara@example.com"}] } ] }
--- logs ---
2026-03-16T21:07:12Z provisioning-service INFO Patch group 0e9a -> 200 OK
2026-03-16T21:07:13Z provisioning-service WARN Patch user 00u1a2b3 -> 403 Forbidden: insufficient_scope
```

sam_infra: 403 on PATCH /Users with "insufficient_scope" usually means the Okta/IdP token used for SCIM has lost `scim:write`. On merges the app permissions sometimes get reset to `scim:read scim:groups` only. Can we confirm the reported token scopes?

jenna_sre: If the token can't write, our mapping job may treat the membership check as a removal and remove the mapped role locally. Need repro steps. @provision-bot any recent deploys to provisioning-service that changed deprovision behavior?

provision-bot: deploy: provisioning-service v3.9.2 rolled 2026-03-16T21:05:00Z. No schema changes in this roll. Noted uptick in 4xx for external-id normalization jobs across a few tenants.

alex_support: Customer UI shows users in the group list returned by SCIM but the role mapping job logs show a "member_missing" path that triggers role removal. That suggests the group-to-role mapper is treating any non-200 on user patch as absence. We should avoid immediate removals on 4xx.

sam_infra: Quick repro steps I used:
1) Create Okta token scoped `scim:read scim:groups` (no scim:write).
2) Run our sync curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/scim+json" -X PATCH https://scim.redwood.example/Users/00u1a2b3 -d '{...}'`
Result: 403 Forbidden with body `{"detail":"insufficient_scope"}`. With token containing `scim:write` the same request returns 200 and mapping proceeds normally. Sending my curl and output to the ticket.

maria_cs: I've asked Clearwave to rotate the token and grant `scim:write` and to re-run a full sync. Opened ticket INC-4721 and added them to a support session tomorrow. Also requested an Okta export of the app permission set to confirm the merge changed scopes.

jenna_sre: I'll open a PR to add an explicit pre-sync scope check (fail-safe) and change the mapper to mark users as "sync-failed" instead of removing roles on any 4xx. Marking this P2. @alex_support please follow up with the customer to confirm token rotation schedule.

alex_support: Will follow up tomorrow and update INC-4721. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
